text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Robeco group loses some four billion guilders in invested capital in 1996 as investors exit its funds. (p1)
- Around half of Dutch capital providers would favour a flotation of Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport. (p1)
- Retail and services group Vendex takes over French temp agency Bis and plans separate listing for its employment services arm Vedior. (p1)
- Brewer Heineken to step up capacity at its Zoeterwoude and Den Bosch breweries. (p3)
- Vacancies in the Amsterdam office market down by 50 percent to 176,000 square meters in 1996. (p3)
- De Boer supermarkets boosts sales by more than six percent in 1996. (p5)
- Packaging giant Van Leer starts new steel drum production plant in Belize, Central America. (p5)
- Construction industry books three percent higher turnover in 1996 after a cold start. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Endemol Entertainment acquires all shares in VSB Circustheater in Scheveningen, upping its stake from 33.3 percent. (p2)
- Rabobank increases its workforce by 2,500 to 39,900 in 1995. (p2)
- Banking payments alliance Interpay orders eight million smart cards on top of first order of four million cards from French concern Bull. (p2)
- Uni-Invest makes public bid for property fund Enhobel. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch cheese export increases two percent to new record of 550,000 tonnes in 1996. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange posts new high of 652.8. (p1)
- Publisher De Telegraaf's Limburg-based subsidiary to acquire regional publisher of free sheets. (p23)
- European Commission to probe into Dutch government subsidies to Philips Semiconductors. (p25)
TROUW
- Amsterdam chief of police Eric Nordholt pleads for cities to be safer still. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Flower auctions in the Netherlands see total sales rise 6.4 pct to 5.75 billion guilders in 1996. (p11)
- Builder NBM-Amstelland seals takeover of Hague-based building firm HABO. (p11)
